content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"The blind consensus reads 'virgin' symbolically as purity, chastity, and exclusive covenant fidelity to God, applied corporately to God's people (virgin Israel/Zion; the Church as pure bride betrothed to Christ), with the Marian literal-prophetic usage treated as the dominant non-symbolic application and eschatological readiness (Matt 25) as a common sub-reading.","book_summary":"The book defines the virgin as 'the espoused' — one legally betrothed to one husband while the wedding is still future. The emphasis is on covenant standing rather than moral attainment: the law counts a betrothed virgin as already a wife (Deut 22), 'the virgin of Israel' names the ten-tribe house re-espoused after her divorce, and plural 'virgins' (Ps 45; Matt 25) are the bride's companions who follow her in, not the bride herself. Opposite: harlot.","consensus_core_identification":"Virgin = purity and undivided covenant faithfulness; corporately, God's people as the pure bride betrothed to God/Christ, free from spiritual adultery.","book_core_identification":"Virgin = the espoused/betrothed party in a covenant marriage awaiting the wedding — a legal-covenantal status ('already counted a wife'), specifically the re-espoused ten-tribe house of Israel; plural virgins are the bride's attendant companions.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The book keeps the consensus's central bridal-covenant referent but redraws boundaries in three ways: (1) it shifts the defining feature from moral/spiritual purity ('attainment') to legal betrothal status ('covenant standing'), explicitly rejecting the purity-as-achievement framing the consensus centers; (2) it narrows 'virgin of Israel' from God's people generally to the divorced-and-re-espoused ten-tribe northern house specifically; (3) it reclassifies the plural virgins of Matthew 25 and Psalm 45 as the bride's companions rather than the bride/church itself, whereas the consensus reads the ten virgins as professing believers awaiting their bridegroom as bride-figures.","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"Both readings identify the virgin within the same marital-covenant frame (betrothal to one husband, 2 Cor 11:2 cited by both), so the central referent survives. But the book materially alters the extension and conditions: virginity is not purity per se but espousal standing prior to the wedding, 'virgin of Israel' is fixed to the ten tribes after divorce, and plural virgins are demoted from bride to bridal retinue. These are real boundary disagreements (especially the Matt 25 reclassification and the standing-not-attainment shift), not mere wording, yet they do not replace or contradict the consensus's core bridal-fidelity identification. Hence REFINED, not DIVERGENT.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book's 'covenant standing, not attainment' framing plus the singular/plural bride-vs-companions distinction so restructures the symbol that it functionally replaces the consensus's purity-centered identification, warranting DIVERGENT — particularly since the consensus reads the Matt 25 virgins as the waiting church itself, while the book denies they are the bride. However, the shared betrothed-bride referent (2 Cor 11:2) keeps the cores compatible rather than contradictory.","confidence":"high"}
